en: Did you visit grandmother's house yesterday?
Yes, I went together with my mother.
Did grandmother like it a lot?
Yes, she received the gift and was very glad.

bg-d-04-01.q: Who went to grandmother's house yesterday?
options: The second speaker and their mother
bg-d-04-01.why: The speaker answers '어머니와 함께 다녀왔어요' (I went together with my mother).

bg-d-04-01.q: How did grandmother react to the gift?
options: She was very glad and liked it
bg-d-04-01.why: The passage states '선물을 받으시고 정말 기뻐하셨어요' (She received the gift and was very glad).
The past honorific form is -(으)셨어요 → 좋아하셨어요.

bg-d-04-01.q: State that the teacher went to the hospital yesterday using 선생님께서, 어제, and 가셨어요.
bg-d-04-01.why: The past honorific for 가다 is 가셨어요.

items: Express past actions of senior persons with -(으)셨어요
Distinguish present -(으)세요 from past -(으)셨어요 based on time context

ko: 손님 여러분, 오늘 회의에 대표님께서 참석하십니다.
en: Ladies and gentlemen, the representative is attending today's meeting.
He will arrive here at two in the afternoon.
Understood, I will finish preparing the meeting room.

bg-d-04-02.q: Who is attending the meeting today?
bg-d-04-02.why: The announcement states '오늘 회의에 대표님께서 참석하십니다' (The representative is attending today's meeting).

bg-d-04-02.q: What time will the representative arrive?
bg-d-04-02.why: The speaker confirms '오후 두 시에 이곳으로 오십니다' (He will arrive here at two in the afternoon).

bg-d-04-02.hint: He will arrive here at two in the afternoon.
bg-d-04-02.why: Formal honorific statement combines stem 오- with -십니다 → 오십니다.

bg-d-04-02.q: Write a formal sentence saying that the department head arrives shortly using 부장님께서 and 도착하십니다.

items: Use -(으)십니다 / -(으)십니까 in formal settings, announcements, and presentations
Avoid mistakenly attaching -시- to inanimate objects

en: Sir/Ma'am, what beverage would you like?
Would you also like to order dessert?
No, I will only have coffee.

bg-d-04-03.q: What beverage does the customer order?
bg-d-04-03.why: The customer answers '따뜻한 아메리카노 한 잔 부탁합니다' (One warm Americano, please).
The customer declines: '아니요, 커피만 마실게요' (No, I will only have coffee).

items.en: would you like to eat/drink (formal offer)

bg-d-04-03.hint: Sir/Ma'am, what beverage would you like?
bg-d-04-03.why: -(으)시겠어요? offers something politely to a customer or someone senior.

bg-d-04-03.q: Politely offer tea to a customer using 차 and 드시겠어요.
bg-d-04-03.why: -(으)시겠어요? expresses a considerate and polite offer.

items: Ask preferences or offer choices using -(으)실래요? and -(으)시겠어요?

ko: 네, 잘 다녀왔습니다. 사장님께서는 회의실에 계십니까?
en: Manager, did your business trip go well yesterday?
Yes, it went well. Is the president in the meeting room?
Yes, he is currently speaking with a guest in the meeting room.
I see. I will go see him after the meeting finishes.

bg-d-04-04.q: Where did the manager go yesterday?
bg-d-04-04.why: The colleague asks '어제 출장 잘 다녀오셨어요?' (Did your business trip go well yesterday?).

bg-d-04-04.q: What is the president doing in the meeting room?
bg-d-04-04.why: The colleague explains '지금 회의실에서 손님과 이야기하십니다' (He is currently speaking with a guest).

items.en: to visit / go and come back (hon.)

bg-d-04-04.hint: Did your business trip go well yesterday?

bg-d-04-04.q: Ask a colleague if the director is in the office right now using 사장님께서 and 계세요.
bg-d-04-04.why: Use 계세요 when asking about the location of a senior person.

items: Switch between -(으)세요, -(으)셨어요, and -(으)십니다 depending on tense and setting
Coordinate honorific nouns with matching verb endings in workplace situations
